jsonld.description: The leisure version: the full English cooked when nobody has anywhere to be, with the additions that only a slow morning justifies — bacon taken to full shatter over low heat, tomatoes roasted to jam, homemade beans if the tin isn't good enough, crumpets or muffins fork-split and toasted in the bacon fat, and the eggs done as a proper basted finale. Where the café fry-up optimises speed, the Sunday version optimises depth — every component gets the extra minutes that turn good into memorable, and the two of you sit down to a plate that took a morning and deserved it.

skeleton:
Sunday Full English for Two

British · Medium · Serves 2 (generously)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The leisure version: the full English cooked when nobody has anywhere to be, with the additions that only a slow morning justifies — bacon taken to full shatter over low heat, tomatoes roasted to jam, homemade beans if the tin isn't good enough, crumpets or muffins fork-split and toasted in the bacon fat, and the eggs done as a proper basted finale. This is the same architecture as the classic master, but unhurried: the timing map runs to an hour, the heat runs lower throughout, and the plate earns one extra component for its patience. Where the café fry-up optimises speed, the Sunday version optimises depth — every component gets the extra minutes that turn good into memorable, and the two of you sit down to a plate that took a morning and deserved it.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The works

  • a good butcher's Cumberland if the morning allows

The slow additions

To serve

- **The reverse clock, relaxed edition:** this version starts with the tomatoes (they want 35 minutes, not the weekday's 15), runs the bacon slow, and lets the beans simmer while everything else finishes. Total about an hour with the last 10 minutes busy and the first 40 minutes nearly hands-off. - **Warm the plates and set the table now** — plates at the lowest oven (about 100 °C), sauce bottles out, the paper's good section chosen. The Sunday fry-up includes its own unhurried staging. - **Fork-split the crumpets or muffins** (never knife — the torn surface holds the fat) and leave them cut-face up, ready for the pan's final minutes.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Tomatoes: 35-minute jam, not 15-minute blister — the marker of the leisure version.
  • Bacon: full amber shatter at low heat; sausage: slow-browned 15 minutes.
  • Crumpets: fork-split, fried cut-face in sausage-bacon fat until crisped and drunk through.
  • Eggs: basted finale, running yolks; the whole plate landing hot after a slow morning.

Sunday Full English for Two

Prep: 20 minutes · Cook: 40 minutes · Total: About 1 hour · Serves 2 (generously)

Ingredients

The works

  • 4 pork sausages (320 g), pricked once each — a good butcher's Cumberland if the morning allows
  • 6 rashers (300 g) smoked back bacon
  • 4 thick slices (200 g) black pudding
  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 2 medium vine tomatoes (250 g), halved
  • 150 g chestnut mushrooms, halved
  • 300 g homemade British-style baked beans, or 200 g the best tinned beans you can buy
  • 2 crumpets or 2 fork-split English muffins (about 120 g)

The slow additions

  • 15 ml / 14 g olive oil
  • 20 g butter, plus extra for the crumpets
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 1 tsp (2 g) brown sugar, for the tomatoes
  • 5 g fresh thyme
  • 10 ml mushroom ketchup, stirred into the beans

To serve

  • Brown breakfast sauce, tomato ketchup, builder's tea or proper coffee, and the Sunday paper

Instructions

  1. **The slow-roasted tomatoes — 35 minutes at 160 °C.** Halve the tomatoes through the equator, salt them lightly, and rest cut-side up 10 minutes while the oven heats; blot. Sit them cut-face up in a small roasting dish with the oil, the sugar, the thyme, and a grind of pepper. Roast 30–35 minutes until deeply slumped, their cavities reduced to jam. Checkpoint — the tomatoes have collapsed by a third, their edges wrinkled and lightly caramelised, and each cavity holds a thick spoonful of concentrated jam — the weekday blistered tomato taken to its fullest expression.
  2. **The sausages — 15 minutes, gentle.** Prick each sausage once. Cook in a pan over medium-low heat (start them dry — good sausages need no oil), turning every 4 minutes, for 15 minutes until evenly, deeply browned. Checkpoint — the skins are taut and browned all over, the meat inside is cooked through and still juicy — the slow turn giving no burst, no grey. Lift to the warm plate.
  3. **The slow bacon — 10 minutes, then the pudding.** Pour off all but a thin slick of the sausage fat (keep what you pour — the crumpets want it). Lay in the bacon over medium-low and cook 4–5 minutes a side — slower than the café's, to a full amber glass on the fat and a deep rose on the eye. Add the black pudding slices for the final 6 minutes, 3 minutes a side. Checkpoint — the bacon's fat is translucent amber and shatters when tapped — the full shatter that only patience reaches — and the meat stays succulent; the pudding is dark-crusted and holding.
  4. **The beans and mushrooms, in parallel — 10 minutes.** While the bacon runs, warm the beans in a small pan with the mushroom ketchup, at the barest simmer. Add the mushrooms to the bacon pan's free space for their last 8 minutes, turning once, until browned and glossed. Checkpoint — the beans are darkened, savoury and thick; the mushrooms are browned whole-face, juicy within.
  5. **Crumpets in the reserved fat, then the eggs — the final 8 minutes.** Take the pan's contents to the warm plates. Melt the butter with a spoon of the reserved sausage fat and fry the crumpets cut-face down 2–3 minutes until the torn surfaces crisp and drink; lift. Then the eggs into the remaining fat over medium heat, basted 2–3 minutes to the butter-basted master's spec — set whites, running yolks, lace edges. Checkpoint — the crumpet's fork-split face is golden and crisp with its fat-soaked pores; the eggs are fringed gold with liquid yolks — the plate's finale, as always.
  6. **Landing — the unhurried plate.** Plates out, warm: tomatoes first (their jam pooled), eggs crowned beside, bacon and sausage arranged, pudding and mushrooms at the sides, crumpets propped against the beans, sauce at the table. Tea or coffee poured, paper at hand. Checkpoint — the plate at arm's length says *occasion* — the jammy tomatoes and fat-fried crumpets marking it as the Sunday version, not the weekday's — and nothing has cooled, because the slow hour ended with a fast, choreographed 10 minutes.

Finish & Plate

Served properly, not wolfed: at the table, the paper within reach, second tea or coffee steeping. The Sunday plate's order of eating is its own ritual — tomato jam first on a forkful of egg, the crumpet torn and dragged through yolk, and the bacon's shatter saved for somewhere near the end, when the plate deserves a finale.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Bacon tough, not shatteringHeat too high, cooked fastMedium-low, 4–5 minutes a side — amber takes patience
Tomatoes dried to leatherOven hot or over-run160 °C, 35 minutes; pull at the slump
Everything hot except the crumpetsCooked before the eggs, left standingCrumpets then eggs, in that order, as the last two acts
Beans scorched in the small panSimmer too fierceThe barest bubble and a stir every few minutes

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Make-ahead:** the tomatoes roast beautifully a day ahead and reheat in 10 minutes at 150 °C — they improve overnight. The beans are the homemade master's whole purpose: a Sunday batch carries three weekends. - **Variation — the Sunday deluxe:** one breakfast Scotch egg (halved) replaces the black pudding — the morning has the time it demands. - **Variation — the champagne version:** a glass of Buck's Fizz alongside; the full English's only acceptable concession to brunch culture. - **For one:** the entire sequence halves cleanly — 2 sausages, 3 rashers, 2 eggs, 1 tomato, 1 crumpet — the timing map unchanged.
